source.title: ProtSAE: Disentangling and Interpreting Protein Language Models via Semantically-Guided Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Xiang-Yu Liu; H. Lei; Yi Liu; Yang Liu; Wei Hu

record.file_problem: The paper text is present in full. Some extracted appendix figure labels and values are garbled; the detailed numeric results in Tables 4–6 are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse autoencoders to a protein language model and reports evidence that dictionary features align with and predict biological concepts, extending this kind of evidence to protein models.
record.gate_note: The paper directly evaluates SAE features through concept relevance and protein-function probing. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry, capacity competition, or whether features are complete or canonical. Steering is deliberately induced and is not treated as evidence of naturally occurring behavior. The main numeric probing results are the AUC values in Tables 4–6; the average relevance comparison is described in text but shown as a figure.
record.test_reason: A methods paper. It assumes linear feature superposition, citing Elhage et al. 2022, and proposes ProtSAE, an SAE supervised with GO annotations and ontology axioms. It trains this on ESM2-15B layer 35 and reports its own method's probing AUC, F1 relevance and loss recovered against Naive, Gated and TopK SAEs. The defined ProtSAE neurons are tied to a supervised concept predictor, so concept alignment is induced by training rather than recovered unsupervised. The baseline-SAE numbers are comparators for the new method, not a test of whether sparse features exist in the model. No version's prediction is put at risk.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that semantic guidance from annotations and ontology axioms yields features more aligned with biological concepts than baseline SAEs, while keeping comparable reconstruction fidelity. They add that ProtSAE's probing performance is comparable to linear probing on raw PLM hidden states, and that its features can steer ESM2 generation toward target concepts.
record.recipe_differences: This is a semantically guided TopK SAE trained with annotation supervision, ontology axioms, forced activations, and feature rescaling—not the toy-model method in the original source. The paper evaluates ESM2-15B and compares ProtSAE with SAE baselines.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported prediction results vary by SAE method, dataset, and L0 sparsity setting. The authors also report ablation effects from removing detach, axiom learning, forced activation bias, or feature rescaling.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes on unsupervised SAE codes of ESM2-15B (Naive, Gated, TopK) give class-centric GO AUC of about 0.47–0.63 (Tables 4–6). This is despite loss recovered up to about 0.99, while a linear probe on raw hidden states reaches ProtSAE-level performance (Table 1). Authors attribute this to semantic loss during SAE training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unsupervised SAE dictionaries on protein LMs may discard concept information that is linearly decodable from the raw activations.

record.problems: Evidence for V4 is limited to ESM2-15B and protein-function/concept tasks. ProtSAE is trained with annotations and domain knowledge, so it is not an unsupervised demonstration of canonical feature recovery. Numeric uncertainty estimates are not reported for the tabled AUC results. Some appendix figure extraction is garbled.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional AUC-independent measures (Fmax, Smin, AUPR, reconstruction fidelity, and ablation outcomes) in Tables 1 and 4–6 and Figures 5–6. They were not separately extracted because the retained rows prioritize the main concept-prediction AUC measure across all reported dataset, method, and L0 conditions. Steering outcomes in Figures 7 and 14 were omitted because they measure deliberately induced generation effects rather than feature recovery itself.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
No test of non-capacity origins of polysemanticity.
No measure of features spread across neurons. No test of whether an unsupervised dictionary recovers sparse features beyond being a benchmark comparator.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.
No comparison of 1-D against multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T3 to uses_without_test/T4, and the reader's V4 supports label is dropped. All rows compare the study's own supervised method with baselines. ProtSAE features are aligned to concepts by construction through a supervised concept predictor, so their probing AUC cannot show natural feature recovery. The claim of SAE 'semantic entanglement' (neurons mixing concepts) is asserted from prior work, not measured. The steering results are induced interventions.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure, or whether it is evidence for superposition.
Tests SAE feature recovery and biological-concept alignment in ESM2-15B, not feature spreading across neurons in broader LLMs or other model families.
Does not establish SAE features as complete, stable, or canonical units; ProtSAE’s semantic guidance uses annotations and domain knowledge.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features or test their geometry.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ProtSAE on ESM2-15B across MFO, BPO, and CCO protein-function datasets and tested L0 settings
reader_labels.reason: ProtSAE features predict biological concepts across all three datasets; its AUC values are reported in rows MFO_P1–MFO_P4, BPO_P1–BPO_P4, and CCO_P1–CCO_P4, with relevance evidence in F1_PROT.
